advances: Ordinary planar areas and actual fixed ray endpoints. The triangle kernel test uses signed vertex offsets at the mark. The ordinary cubic equality test uses normalized edge drops and has a different scope.

proof:
The prescribed-area criterion of [7d1ee06fa4119930](../facts/7d1ee06fa4119930.md) applies to the actual endpoints and sectors. In its notation $D_i=R_iR_{i+1}$ and $E_i=R_{i-1}R_{i+1}$, since determinants of consecutive and next-neighbor direction pairs are both one. Thus its node coefficient is $1/D_{i-1}+1/D_i-1/R_i^2$. Expanding the criterion after $z_i=R_i x_i$ gives
$$
z^\top Lz=\sum_{i=0}^{5}c_i(R_ix_i+R_{i+1}x_{i+1})^2
-\sum_{i=0}^{5}x_i^2-2\sum_{i=0}^{5}x_ix_{i+1}.
$$
Under the period-three identification the last two terms become $-2(x_0+x_1+x_2)^2$. This gives the displayed entries. The restriction of a positive semidefinite form is positive semidefinite. Each core triangle lies in $K$, so $c_iR_iR_{i+1}\le1$ and the off-diagonal entries are nonpositive.

In the triangle case the positive-excess sectors are the three open unique sectors, indexed by $1,3,5$, each containing its corresponding unique vertex. The double sectors are core triangles: the arc between two consecutive rays bounding such a sector has no vertex, and hence is a straight edge segment. Each of the six ray endpoints is strictly inside a triangle edge because no vertex lies on a cutting line. Apply the actual-sector charges from [7d1ee06fa4119930](../facts/7d1ee06fa4119930.md) to the vertex $sP_i+tP_{i+1}$ in each positive sector and zero charges on each core. Since the boundary joins at every endpoint are straight, the turn formula in that fact gives zero slack at each node. The Gram identity of [2fb8b0785692a5b4](../facts/2fb8b0785692a5b4.md) therefore splits $z^\top Lz$ into three independent positive multiples of squares, one on each pair bounding a unique sector. If the two vertex coefficients are $(s,t)$, the edge charges are proportional to $(1/s,1/t)$ and the square vanishes precisely when $(z_i,z_{i+1})$ is proportional to $(t,s)$.

In sectors $5,1,3$ the two coefficients are respectively $(b_{21}/R_5,b_{31}/R_0)$, $(b_{32}/R_1,b_{12}/R_2)$, and $(b_{13}/R_3,b_{23}/R_4)$, by the canonical ray vectors and the identity $\sum_i v_i=0$. On dividing by the radii, the kernel equations become
$$
b_{21}x_5=b_{31}x_0,\qquad
b_{32}x_1=b_{12}x_2,\qquad
b_{13}x_3=b_{23}x_4.
$$
Use $x_5=x_2$, $x_3=x_0$ and $x_4=x_1$. Positivity of the six coefficients makes the only solution zero unless the forward and backward products agree. When they agree, choosing $x_0$ fixes the other two coordinates and gives a one-dimensional kernel. This proves the assertion about $N$.
statement:
Let $K\subset\mathbb R^2$ be a convex body with $0$ in its interior. Index its six rays by the vectors $e_i=(1,0),(0,1),(-1,1),(-1,0),(0,-1),(1,-1)$ in this order, with $i=0,\dots,5$. Write $P_i=R_ie_i$ for the actual boundary endpoint, $W_i$ for the area of $K$ between $P_i,P_{i+1}$, and $c_i=1/(2W_i)$. In the exact sector matrix $L$ of [7d1ee06fa4119930](../facts/7d1ee06fa4119930.md), substitute $z_i=R_i x_i$ and restrict to $x_{i+3}=x_i$. The resulting matrix $N$ on $(x_0,x_1,x_2)$ is positive semidefinite with nonpositive off-diagonal entries. Its coefficients, with matrix indices modulo three and ray indices modulo six, are
$$
\begin{aligned}
N_{ii}&=R_i^2(c_{i-1}+c_i)+R_{i+3}^2(c_{i+2}+c_{i+3})-2,\\
N_{i,i+1}&=c_iR_iR_{i+1}+c_{i+3}R_{i+3}R_{i+4}-2.
\end{aligned}
$$

Suppose $K$ is a triangle with vertices $V_j$ and the three canonical normals $v_1=(1,0)$, $v_2=(0,1)$, $v_3=(-1,-1)$ strictly isolate the respective vertices. Write $v_i\cdot V_i=a_i>0$ and $v_i\cdot V_j=-b_{ij}<0$ for $i\ne j$. Then $N$ is singular if and only if $b_{12}b_{23}b_{31}=b_{13}b_{32}b_{21}$. Its kernel in that case is one-dimensional, and it is positive definite otherwise.
title: The period-three compression of the actual planar sector matrix
